_about: Plain-English layer for the website. Keyed by bet_id. Written for a reader new to physics. Everything here is explanation of rows in data/bets.csv; the judgments and sources live in the CSVs, not here.

astro2010-wfirst.plain_name: WFIRST, now the Roman Space Telescope
astro2010-wfirst.what: A space telescope with a very wide field of view, built to survey huge patches of the sky in infrared light.
astro2010-wfirst.question_plain: Why is the expansion of the universe speeding up, and how common are Earth-like planets?

astro2010-lsst.what: A ground telescope in Chile that photographs the whole southern sky every few nights for ten years, producing a time-lapse movie of the universe.
astro2010-lsst.question_plain: Why is the expansion of the universe speeding up? Also, what changes in the night sky from night to night?

astro2010-explorer.what: Not one telescope but a funding line: extra money so NASA could launch more small, fast, competitively chosen missions during the decade.
astro2010-explorer.question_plain: Can a steady stream of small missions respond quickly to new discoveries?

astro2010-lisa.what: Three spacecraft flying millions of kilometres apart, measuring tiny ripples in space itself (gravitational waves) from colliding giant black holes.
astro2010-lisa.question_plain: Can we hear giant black holes merging, and does Einstein's theory of gravity hold up in that extreme regime?

astro2010-ixo.what: A large X-ray space observatory, planned with Europe and Japan, to see hot gas and black holes.
astro2010-ixo.question_plain: How did the first giant black holes grow, and how does hot gas move through galaxies?

astro2010-msip.what: A funding line at the National Science Foundation for medium-sized telescope and instrument projects, too big for small grants and too small for flagship budgets.
astro2010-msip.question_plain: Can a competitive mid-size funding line keep ground-based astronomy innovating between flagships?

astro2010-gsmt.what: A US share in one of two planned giant ground telescopes with mirrors 25 to 30 metres across (the Giant Magellan Telescope or the Thirty Meter Telescope).
astro2010-gsmt.question_plain: What were the earliest galaxies made of, and can we directly photograph planets around other stars?

astro2010-acta.plain_name: ACTA, a US share of CTA
astro2010-acta.what: A US role in a large array of telescopes that detect the faint blue flashes made when very high-energy gamma rays hit the atmosphere.
astro2010-acta.question_plain: Is dark matter made of particles that annihilate and give off gamma rays?

astro2010-ccat.what: A submillimetre-wave telescope on a high peak in Chile to survey dusty galaxies and star-forming clouds.
astro2010-ccat.question_plain: Where and how did galaxies, stars, and planets form, as seen through cosmic dust?

astro2010-new-worlds-tech.what: Technology development, not a mission: the instruments needed to one day photograph an Earth-like planet around another star.
astro2010-new-worlds-tech.question_plain: What fraction of nearby stars have Earth-like planets, and can we build the tools to image them?

astro2010-inflation-probe-tech.what: Technology development for detectors that could find a faint twist in the oldest light in the universe, a predicted fingerprint of the Big Bang's first instant.
astro2010-inflation-probe-tech.question_plain: Did the universe undergo a burst of faster-than-light expansion (inflation) in its first fraction of a second?

astro2010-spica.what: A Japanese-led cooled infrared space telescope that the US was invited to join as a small partner.
astro2010-spica.question_plain: How do galaxies, stars, and planets form, as seen in the far infrared?

p5-2014-hl-lhc.what: A major upgrade to the Large Hadron Collider in Geneva so it can smash protons together far more often, with the US building magnets and detector parts.
p5-2014-hl-lhc.question_plain: Does the Higgs boson behave exactly as the standard theory predicts, and are there new particles or dark matter hiding at higher energies?

p5-2014-lbnf.what: A beam of neutrinos (ghostly particles that barely interact with matter) fired 1,300 km from Chicago to a giant detector a mile underground in South Dakota.
p5-2014-lbnf.question_plain: Do neutrinos and antineutrinos behave differently, which could explain why the universe is made of matter? And which neutrino is heaviest?

p5-2014-pip-ii.what: A new accelerator at Fermilab to make a much more intense proton beam, the source of neutrinos for DUNE.
p5-2014-pip-ii.question_plain: Can the US produce the world's most intense neutrino beam?

p5-2014-mu2e.what: An experiment at Fermilab looking for a muon (a heavy cousin of the electron) turning directly into an electron, which the standard theory says essentially never happens.
p5-2014-mu2e.question_plain: Is there physics beyond the standard theory that lets a muon become an electron?

p5-2014-muon-g-2.what: A precision measurement of how a muon wobbles in a magnetic field, compared with theory to extraordinary precision.
p5-2014-muon-g-2.question_plain: Does the muon's magnetic wobble differ from prediction, hinting at unknown particles?

p5-2014-lhc-phase-1.what: Intermediate upgrades to the ATLAS and CMS detectors at the LHC to keep them working at higher collision rates before the big upgrade.
p5-2014-lhc-phase-1.question_plain: Can the detectors keep up with the LHC and keep searching for new particles?

p5-2014-ilc.what: A proposed 20 km electron-positron collider in Japan that would study the Higgs boson in clean collisions. The US was to join only if Japan built it.
p5-2014-ilc.question_plain: Does the Higgs boson couple to other particles exactly as predicted?

p5-2014-desi.what: An instrument with 5,000 robotic fibre positioners on a telescope in Arizona, measuring distances to tens of millions of galaxies to map the expansion history of the universe.
p5-2014-desi.question_plain: Is dark energy, the thing pushing the universe apart, constant over time or changing?

p5-2014-lsst.what: The Department of Energy's part of the Rubin Observatory: its 3,200-megapixel camera and the dark energy analysis.
p5-2014-lsst.question_plain: Can measuring billions of galaxy shapes pin down dark energy to one percent?

p5-2014-dm-g2.what: Three underground or shielded experiments (LZ, SuperCDMS, ADMX) waiting for a dark matter particle to bump into ordinary matter.
p5-2014-dm-g2.question_plain: Is dark matter made of heavy particles (WIMPs) or very light ones (axions) that we can catch directly?

p5-2014-dm-g3.what: A follow-on, much larger dark matter detector, planned to be built once the second generation reported.
p5-2014-dm-g3.question_plain: Can we push the search for dark matter all the way to the floor set by neutrinos?

p5-2014-cmb-s4.what: A planned array of telescopes at the South Pole and in Chile with half a million detectors, mapping the afterglow of the Big Bang.
p5-2014-cmb-s4.question_plain: Did the universe begin with a burst of inflation? Its gravitational waves would leave a swirl pattern in the oldest light.

p5-2014-sbn.what: Three liquid-argon detectors in a row along a neutrino beam at Fermilab, looking for a fourth kind of neutrino.
p5-2014-sbn.question_plain: Is there a fourth, 'sterile' neutrino, as some earlier experiments hinted?

p5-2014-pingu.what: A proposed denser cluster of sensors inside the IceCube detector in Antarctic ice, to study low-energy neutrinos.
p5-2014-pingu.question_plain: Which neutrino is heaviest, as read from neutrinos made in the atmosphere?

p5-2014-lar1.what: A proposed mid-sized liquid-argon detector to chase hints of a fourth neutrino. Its near detector became SBND.

p5-2014-chips.what: A cheap water-tank detector sunk in a flooded mine pit in Minnesota, in the path of an existing neutrino beam.
p5-2014-chips.question_plain: Can a very cheap detector add a little to what we know about neutrino masses?

p5-2014-mice.what: A UK-based experiment demonstrating a way to squeeze a beam of muons, a step toward a future muon collider.
p5-2014-mice.question_plain: Can muon beams be cooled enough to build a collider out of them?

p5-2014-nustorm.what: A proposed ring to store muons and use their decays as a precisely known neutrino source.
p5-2014-nustorm.question_plain: Is there a fourth neutrino, tested with a neutrino source whose output is known exactly?

p5-2014-orka.what: A proposed experiment to measure an extremely rare decay of kaons (particles containing a strange quark).
p5-2014-orka.question_plain: Does a rare kaon decay happen at the rate the standard theory predicts?

p5-2014-radar.what: A proposed liquid-argon detector at the far end of an existing neutrino beam in Minnesota.
p5-2014-radar.question_plain: Can an existing beam sharpen our knowledge of how neutrinos change type?

p5-2014-cta.what: A US contribution to the international Cherenkov Telescope Array, which watches for gamma rays from space.
p5-2014-cta.question_plain: Is dark matter annihilating in the centre of our galaxy and giving off gamma rays?
